purpose: Teach: サックス/ダイビング/モデム/ロジック/スロット/エッチ/楽園/着席

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがサックスを吹かれたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran — your father used to play the saxophone when he was young.
lines.style: Soft, gazing inward. Gentle nostalgic draw on the memory. Unhurried pace. Voice settles into the warmth of recollection, like handling something cherished.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ダイビングを試されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and you tried diving back then, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, playful turn-around. Slight tease in the acknowledgment. Eyes crinkling. She matches his wistfulness but gently redirects it — a shared knowing smile in her voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、モデム接続の音、懐かしいぞ
lines.en: Gran — the sound of a modem connecting. Those days feel so far away now.
lines.style: Quieter, more personal. A small smile in the voice. Drawing out the memory of that particular sound with tenderness. Slight wonder at how time has moved.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、商売のロジックを学んでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you learned so much about business then, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle, encouraging. A light nod in her tone — recognizing his growth without making a fuss. Warm and knowing, like she saw something in him even then.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お祖母ちゃんちにスロット遊具があったぞ
lines.en: Gran — there was even a slot machine in your grandmother's house. Those were the days.
lines.style: Amused remembrance, a touch of mischief. Light laugh threaded through. Voice brightens slightly — he's enjoying this detail. Unhurried, savoring the absurdity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、エッチな話題は遠ざけてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You always kept the conversation proper and respectful, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Teasing affection with an edge of gentle sarcasm. She knows exactly what he's doing. A small laugh underneath. Warm rebuke wrapped in tenderness.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「楽園」のような故郷を語られたぞ
lines.en: Gran — your father used to speak about our hometown like it was paradise itself.
lines.style: Reverent, almost wistful. Voice softens on the word paradise. Slow, measured pace. The kind of remembrance that holds something sacred in it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お客様の着席を礼儀正しくお迎えされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you welcomed every guest with such courtesy and grace, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm finality. A gentle smile closing a conversation. Affectionate acknowledgment. Voice trails softly, settling into contentment. This is her last word — it's a benediction.
